title: A Migration Feasibility Study Can Turn an Uncertain Re-Design into a Measurable Engineering Project
gist: A promotional piece for IN2FAB's Migration Feasibility Study, which tests how much of an analog/mixed-signal IP block's existing schematic and physical layout can be reused when porting to a new process using its OSIRIS technology. It argues the study replaces estimates with design-specific evidence before committing to migration versus redesign.

themes.theme: Layout reuse as the case for migration over redesign

insights.claim: For analog and mixed-signal IP, restarting from the schematic overlooks the engineering knowledge embedded in the existing physical layout (device sizing, matching, symmetry, routing, shielding, placement, hierarchy), so preserving it could reduce the effort of porting proven IP to a new process.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Vendor claim that automated layout migration can undercut full redesign cost for legacy analog IP.
insights.locator: Moving semiconductor IP to a new process technology

insights.claim: IN2FAB's OSIRIS technology is designed to migrate both schematics and physical layouts while preserving design hierarchy and structure.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Product capability statement; no performance or customer results are given.

insights.claim: A process-node or foundry comparison cannot reveal design-specific challenges, because each block has its own devices, parameters, PCells, vias and dependence on technology-specific design rules; the study examines which devices map, where parameter limits arise and what layout can be preserved.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Pilot-block testing gives evidence of migration feasibility before large engineering commitments.
insights.locator: Test the Design, Not Just the Process Comparison

insights.claim: IN2FAB's technology can automate device mapping, PCell handling, layer and via translation, layout transformation and hierarchy preservation, while other structures still need engineering judgment, modification or redesign.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Automation covers repetitive tech-dependent steps only; residual manual effort limits savings.

insights.claim: Successful translation is only a milestone: the migrated design still requires verification against its intended performance and target-process requirements.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Migration does not remove verification cost; account for it in any effort estimate.
insights.locator: Successful translation is an important milestone

insights.claim: A representative pilot block provides a basis for estimating effort, resources, schedules and verification needs, and for prioritising migration across a broader IP portfolio.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Converts an uncertain re-design into a measurable project, useful for companies with large legacy IP portfolios.

insights.claim: Customers can use IN2FAB's migration technology internally, engage IN2FAB for engineering services, or combine both, indicating a mixed software-licence and services business model.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Revenue mix of tool licences versus services is the point to watch for this vendor.
insights.locator: The findings can also guide the delivery approach

insights.claim: The migrate-or-redesign decision affects cost, schedule, engineering capacity and time to market.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Framing used to sell an evidence-first step before a large commitment.
insights.quote: The decision to migrate or redesign affects cost, schedule, engineering capacity, and time to market.
